slides.0.title: Industry and market
slides.0.subtitle: The figures vary widely, so start with the structure
slides.1.title: Scale: why the figures disagree
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Area
slides.1.highlights.0.content: One source gives about 31,000 ha of vineyard in 2008, just over half for wine. Others give 14,000–18,000 ha, or a few thousand hectares counting wine grapes only
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Why they differ
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Whether table grapes are included, different years, and continued shrinking in recent years. This course found no recent official statistics
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Output
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Reports from the 2000s usually give 300,000–400,000 hl a year, with a peak of 600,000 hl in 2007. These are press figures
slides.1.content: Just remember the order of magnitude: far below the protectorate peak.
slides.2.title: Who makes the wine
slides.2.highlights.0.title: The cooperative union
slides.2.highlights.0.content: The UCCV, the central union of wine cooperatives, trades as "Les Vignerons de Carthage". Reports from 2008–2010 put it at about two-thirds of national output
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Joint ventures
slides.2.highlights.1.content: From the late 1990s, French, German, Italian and Austrian capital came in through joint ventures, bringing new equipment and international varieties
slides.2.highlights.2.title: History as a brand
slides.2.highlights.2.content: The Magon wine is named after the Carthaginian agronomist Mago, which shows how much history is used in marketing
slides.2.content: One big cooperative union plus a handful of joint ventures is the basic shape of the industry.
slides.3.title: Where it is sold
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Exports
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Reports from around 2009: exports about 40% of output, mainly to Germany and France, followed by Switzerland, Belgium, the US, Canada and Russia
slides.3.highlights.1.title: At home
slides.3.highlights.1.content: The same reports estimate home consumption at about 2.2 litres a head a year. Tunisia is mostly Muslim, but alcohol is sold legally
slides.3.highlights.2.title: The AOC share
slides.3.highlights.2.content: A common claim is that about 70% is sold as AOC, a fifth of it labelled "premier cru". This course found no legal basis for "premier cru", so the figure is not tested
slides.3.content: Exports lean on Germany and France and the home market is small. Those are the two features of the Tunisian market.
